items.description: Testing Library helpers that skip UI SDK's live regions: getToast, queryToast, queryToasts, queryAlerts, queryStatuses, isAnnouncer, ignoreAnnouncer, readAnnouncements and resetAnnouncer.
items.docs: For tests only. UI SDK announces through two hidden live regions in <body> (`role="status"` and `role="alert"`, marked `data-ui-sdk-announcer`) that keep the last text they announced, so `getByRole("alert")` and `getByText` can find them after a toast has closed. Find toasts with `getToast(text)` or `[data-slot="toast"]`, query inside `within(screen.getByRole("region", { name: "Notifications" }))`, pass `{ ignore: ignoreAnnouncer }` to text queries, and call `resetAnnouncer()` in `afterEach`.

items.name: theme
items.title: Theme
items.description: Semantic color tokens plus shape, density and surface tokens. The default look: rounded, roomy, soft shadows.
items.docs: Add `@layer ui-sdk;` as the first line of your global stylesheet, above `@import "tailwindcss"`, so your styles win over UI SDK's behavior CSS. The theme asks for Geist Variable and falls back to the system font: `npx shadcn add @eskais/font-geist` installs it (or add `@fontsource-variable/geist` and `@import "@fontsource-variable/geist";` yourself). It brings `@eskais/utils`, whose `cn` knows the theme's utilities (`text-meta`, `gap-items`, `rounded-surface`…); with another `cn`, `cn("text-meta", "text-muted-foreground")` drops the size. If `shadcn init` already wrote `lib/utils.ts`, add with `--overwrite` so ours replaces it.

items.name: spinner
items.title: Spinner
items.description: An SVG spinner in currentColor, sized like an icon (sm, md, lg). Decorative by default; with a label it becomes a role=status region. Pulses instead of spinning under reduced motion.
items.docs: Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`): put it next to text that already says what is loading, or inside a Button, which shows it while pending. Pass `label` (in the page's language) when the spinner is the only sign of loading: it becomes `role="status"` with a screen-reader-only label.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: UI SDK Button with variants: async pending state, a loading prop with a spinner, focusable-when-disabled, link rendering, and a tooltip with its name (and shortcut) on an icon button. ButtonLink is a Link with the Button look, for calls to action that navigate.
items.docs:
Return a Promise from `onClick` and the button stays pending until it settles: `aria-busy`, presses ignored, focus kept, a spinner, and `pendingAnnouncement` after a second. For work the button didn't start (a form submit, a mutation elsewhere), pass `loading`: it renders the same state through `disabled` + `focusableWhenDisabled`, as UI SDK documents for external pending flags. The spinner takes the leading icon's place, or sits centered over the label, so the width never changes. `shortcut="u"` presses the button from the keyboard while it is mounted, in the enclosing `ShortcutScope`, shows the keys after the label and sets `aria-keyshortcuts` (`shortcutHint={false}` hides them, `shortcutDescription` names it in the `ShortcutsDialog`).

### Icon buttons

`size="icon"` requires `aria-label`, and the button shows that label in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus (never on touch), with the `shortcut` keys after it instead of inside the square. The tooltip labels the button with the same text, so screen readers hear the name once, and agents see only the button. Tooltips group without a provider: once one is open, the next opens at once, so moving along a toolbar reads as one tooltip. `tooltip={false}` turns it off when a visible label sits beside the button; `tooltip="Moves it to the trash"` describes the button with other text, and `tooltip={{ content, side, align }}` places it. A text button gets a tooltip only when you pass one. A natively `disabled` icon button can't be focused, so it gets none: `focusableWhenDisabled` keeps it. `DialogTrigger`, `DialogClose`, `DrawerTrigger`, `DrawerClose`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverClose`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`, `ToastClose` and `Toggle` take the same `size="icon"`, `aria-label` and `tooltip`. A Button that is already a `TooltipTrigger`'s `render` keeps that tooltip. The `eskais/icon-button-needs-label` lint rule (in `@eskais/lint-rules`) flags an icon-only Button or Toggle without `size="icon"` and an `aria-label`.

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: UI SDK Field parts: label, description and validation errors wired to the control; FieldSet with a legend that names the group.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: UI SDK Input, InputGroup and InputClear (clears and returns focus).

items.name: search-field
items.title: Search Field
items.description: Search landmark built with definePrimitive: Enter runs onSearch, Escape clears only when there is text, and agents get a submit action.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: UI SDK Dialog parts: focus trap, Escape, focus restore, dismissible and controller support.
items.docs: Focus returns to whatever opened the dialog. `DialogContent` records the focused element as it opens, so focus still comes back when the dialog leaves the page while open (`{open && <Dialog open>…</Dialog>}`) and when a field inside has React's `autoFocus`, which takes focus before UI SDK records where it came from. To choose the first field, pass `initialFocus` to `DialogContent` (a selector like `"#name"`, an element, or a function), not `autoFocus`: it is how UI SDK decides where focus starts, and after a touch press it focuses the dialog itself so no on-screen keyboard pops up. Prefer keeping the `Dialog` mounted and driving `open`: an unmounted dialog skips its exit transition. `finalFocus` overrides where focus returns; `"none"` leaves it alone, also on unmount. While the dialog animates out, its backdrop and content are inert (UI SDK) and `pointer-events: none`, so the first click on the page after closing lands. ConfirmDialog, FormDialog, CommandDialog and Drawer share all of this.

items.name: confirm-dialog
items.title: Confirm Dialog
items.description: UI SDK AlertDialog with an async confirm action: pending, no double submit, closes on success, inline error on failure, data-agent-confirm for destructive actions.
items.docs: `<ConfirmDialog trigger title description confirmLabel onConfirm>`: a returned Promise keeps it open and pending, a rejection shows its message (`renderError`). `tone="destructive"` requires `agentConfirm`. Children render as a callout under the description, an Alert in the dialog's tone (`destructive`, or `info` for the default tone; `calloutTone` overrides) that screen readers hear with the description. `labels={{ cancel }}` names the cancel button, "Cancel" by default; `cancelLabel` is deprecated.

items.name: form
items.title: Form
items.description: Forms on react-hook-form with a Standard Schema (Zod, Valibot, Effect): FormField binds one registry control by name, pending submit, server errors mapped to fields, a live root error, focus on the first invalid field, and messages in any language or i18n library.
items.docs: `<Form schema defaultValues onSubmit messages label>` with `<FormField name label description required>` around one control: Input, Textarea, NumberInput, Select, Combobox, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup, Slider, DatePicker, SegmentedControl, ToggleGroup or TokenInput bind by `name` (no `control` or `render`); `bind` or `render` for anything else, `useFormField()` inside a custom control. Give every field a default value. A field the schema rejects when empty (probed synchronously with the default values; Zod, Valibot and ArkType report every issue) gets a required marker, an `aria-hidden` asterisk in `text-destructive`, and its control `required`; `required` forces it, `required={false}` drops it. `requiredLabel` on the Form or field adds words for screen readers, like "required" in the page's language, which join the field's name; unset, screen readers announce the control's `required` state instead. `const { Form, FormField, useFormInstance, useFormWatch, useFormFieldArray } = createForm<typeof schema>()` types `name` against the schema's input; they are the same components. `onSubmit(values, { setError })` may return a Promise: the submit Button shows `loading`, fields are disabled (`disableWhilePending={false}` keeps them), a second submit is ignored. Throw a `FormServerError(message, fieldErrors)`, `{ fieldErrors, message }` or a Standard Schema issue list (`toFormErrors`) to put errors on fields and in `<FormRootError />` (an `Alert tone="destructive" live`); any other error shows its message there. Focus then goes to the first invalid field, or to the root error. Messages: `messages={formMessagesEs}`, a dictionary, or a function of the issue for i18next, FormatJS or Lingui (`createFormMessages(t)` makes one from `t(key, params)`, keys `form.<code>`); `FormField messages` wins over the form's. An issue is `{ code, field, label, params, message }`; codes: `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `min`, `max` (params `min`/`max`), `email`, `url`, `pattern`, `invalid`, `server`, or a schema message that looks like a key (`form.email.taken`), or a server error's own `code`. Schemas whose issues carry no code or params (Effect Schema) write the code into the message: `formIssueMessage("form.name.min", { min: 3 })` gives `@@form:form.name.min|{"min":3}` (a reserved prefix, never read from prose), read back as code `form.name.min` with `params.min` and no `message`; a built-in code works the same way (`formIssueMessage("minLength", { min: 3 })` gets the built-in translations). Unmatched, the key shows without its params. Inside a Form, `useFormInstance<Values>()` returns the typed react-hook-form instance (`trigger`, `setValue`, `getValues`, `control`, `formState`); its `watch` re-renders the Form, so read a live value with `useFormWatch(name)`. `useFormFieldArray(name, options)` is `useFieldArray` bound to the form: key rows by `field.id` (or, when the items carry their own `id`, by the property `keyName: "fieldKey"` names) and name their fields `items.${index}.title`. `form-context.ts` is internal; import only from `form`. Agents fill fields through their own parts and call the form's `submit` and `reset` when it has a `label`; `<FormActions tone="destructive" confirm="…">` puts `data-agent-confirm` on the submit button and hides the form's `submit` from agents. `FormActions disabled` (submit and cancel), `submitDisabled` (submit only) and `pending` (the pending look) reflect a busy state outside the form; while set, the form doesn't submit.

items.name: form-dialog
items.title: Form Dialog
items.description: A Form inside a Dialog: a scrolling body with a sticky footer, Escape and outside presses blocked while pending, closes on success and returns focus, asks before discarding unsaved changes, and an optional review step before submitting.
items.docs: `<FormDialog trigger title description size schema defaultValues onSubmit submitLabel cancelLabel>` with `FormField`s as children; or control it with `open`/`onOpenChange(open, details)`, where `details.reason` is `submit`, `cancel`, `escape`, `outside` or `dismiss` (any other dismissal) on close and `trigger` on open, with UI SDK's own reason in `details.dialogReason`; `onOpenChangeComplete(open, details)` runs once the transition ends. After `confirmDiscard`, the reason is the one that asked. It takes every `Form` prop (`messages`, `disableWhilePending`…) and `FormActions`' `tone`, `confirm` and `secondaryAction`. While `onSubmit` runs, Escape, outside presses and Cancel do nothing; it closes when `onSubmit` resolves and focus returns to the trigger, or to `returnFocus` (UI SDK `finalFocus`). A thrown error keeps it open with the errors on the fields and in the root error. `confirmDiscard="Discard changes?"` asks before Escape, an outside press or Cancel closes it with unsaved changes (`discardLabel`, `keepEditingLabel`). `reviewStep={{ render: (values) => …, editLabel, confirmLabel }}`: submit validates and shows the review, edit returns to the fields with the values kept, confirm runs `onSubmit`; a field error from the server returns to the fields. `prepare(values, { form })` runs before the review with the submit pending and returns `{ values }` to review and submit other values, which are also written into the form so Edit shows them, or `{ error }` (any shape `onSubmit` throws) to stay on the fields; values it sets through `form` without returning any are parsed again and reviewed, and returned `values` win over them; `editable` (`false`, or a function of `{ values, error, pending }`) hides the edit button, for example after a failed delivery; `title` replaces the dialog's title while reviewing, or `title: (step) => …` with `"form"` or `"review"`. The body scrolls between the header and the actions, and on narrow screens it is a bottom sheet.

items.name: step-dialog
items.title: Step Dialog
items.description: A multi-step form on one schema, in a Dialog or inline: a progress list with aria-current, Next validates only the current step, Back keeps values, focus moves to each step's heading, and a failed submit returns to the step with the error.
items.docs: `<StepDialog trigger title description schema defaultValues steps onSubmit labels>`, or `<StepForm>` inline with the same props (no dialog ones). `steps` is `{ id, title, description?, render: (form) => …, fields?, validate? }[]`: `render` returns the step's `FormField`s, `fields` lists what Next validates (the step's mounted fields by default) and `validate(values)` runs after them, returning nothing or an error in any shape `onSubmit` throws. Next and Enter validate only the current step; Back keeps every value; the last step's button submits the whole schema through `onSubmit`, with Form's error mapping. A failed validation or a server field error returns to the step that holds the field (`fields`, or the fields seen there). Focus moves to the step's heading (`h2` inline, `h3` in the dialog, `headingLevel` on StepForm) on Next and Back, and to the first invalid field after an error. The progress is an `<ol>` with `aria-current="step"` on the current step, named by `labels.progress`. `step`/`defaultStep` and `onStepChange(id, { index, previous, direction })` (`next`, `back` or `error`). `labels` (`next`, `back`, `submit`, `progress`, and `cancel` in the dialog) default to English. Agents fill each step's fields by label and press Next, Back and the submit button by name. StepDialog closes when `onSubmit` resolves, ignores Escape, outside presses and Cancel while pending, and starts over each time it opens. `onOpenChange(open, details)` says why in `details.reason`: `submit`, `done`, `cancel`, `escape`, `outside`, `dismiss`, or `trigger` when it opens. Opt in to `resultStep={{ title, render: (result, { close, restart }) => … }}` to show what `onSubmit` resolved with inside the dialog instead of closing it: focus moves to the result's heading, Done (`labels.done`) and Escape close it, and `restart` starts over from the first step with the default values.

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: Card parts: a titled card renders as a section labelled by its title, with an eyebrow, a top-end action slot, a heading level on the title and card, dashed or bare surfaces.
items.docs: A `Card` renders `<section>`; once it holds a `CardTitle` it gets `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title, so it is a named region. Give the title `headingLevel` to make it a heading. `CardEyebrow` sits above the title, `CardAction` at the top end of `CardHeader`. The header is a container (`@container/card-header`): the action sits beside the title, which keeps at least 8rem, once the header has 17rem of content (a card of about 20rem), and wraps below the title, start-aligned, in a narrower card. Its buttons wrap among themselves rather than overflow. `surface` is `card` (default), `dashed` or `none`. To keep a card out of the landmarks (a card per list item), pass `render={<div />}` or `render={<li />}`.

items.name: section
items.title: Section
items.description: A titled block of a page, composed from Card: eyebrow, title at a heading level, description, top-end action, footer; card, bare or dashed (create tile) surfaces and sm or md padding.
items.docs: `<Section title="Members" action={<Button>Invite</Button>}>…</Section>` renders a `section` named by its title (an `h2` unless `headingLevel` says otherwise). `surface="none"` keeps the heading without a box, `surface="dashed"` is the outlined tile for creating something. `padding="sm"` tightens dense dashboards.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: Presentational badge: tone (neutral, info, success, warning, destructive) for meaning, variant (default, secondary, outline) for an untoned look. Tone values passed as variant still work but are deprecated.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: UI SDK Tabs: arrow-key navigation, automatic or manual activation, controller support, a selected state that reads at 3:1, and a list that scrolls when its tabs don't fit, with edge fades and pointer-only scroll buttons.
items.docs: `TabsList scrollable` is `"auto"` by default: a horizontal list that overflows scrolls, fades the edges it can scroll to, and on fine pointers shows a button at each of those edges. The buttons are `aria-hidden`, out of the tab order and hidden from agents, since arrow keys, Home and End reach every tab and UI SDK scrolls the selected one into view. It reads the direction from the page, so it works under `dir="rtl"`. `scrollLabels` renames the buttons; `scrollable={false}` keeps a plain list.

items.name: collapsible
items.title: Collapsible
items.description: UI SDK Collapsible: disclosure with aria-expanded, animated height, controller support and a rotating chevron icon.

items.name: scroll-area
items.title: Scroll Area
items.description: UI SDK ScrollArea: native scrolling with styled scrollbars, edge state and follow-to-end, keyboard-reachable when it overflows.

items.name: separator
items.title: Separator
items.description: UI SDK Separator: horizontal or vertical, announced or decorative.

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: UI SDK Avatar with sizes: a real img that falls back to initials while loading or on error.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: Presentational loading placeholder, hidden from assistive technology, that stops pulsing under reduced motion.

items.name: empty
items.title: Empty
items.description: Presentational empty-state parts in three sizes (inline, panel, page): media, title, description and actions.

items.name: states
items.title: States
items.description: Screen states that never lie: LoadingState (spinner or skeleton, busy, label for screen readers), ErrorState (alert, retry, collapsible details) and DataState, which picks loading, error, empty or your content from a status and never shows empty while pending or after an error.
items.docs: One item, three components (`error-state`, `loading-state`, `data-state`), since DataState renders the other two and Empty by default. `<DataState status data error onRetry labels={{ errorTitle, retry, emptyTitle }}>{(data) => …}</DataState>` works with any data library: map its status to `pending`, `error` or `success`. Visible copy has no default: the types require `errorTitle` and `emptyTitle` (and `retry` with `onRetry`) unless you pass `renderError` and `empty`. `loading` and `refreshing` are screen-reader labels and default to English. It picks one state from `status`: `error` shows the error; `success` shows empty when `isEmpty(data)` holds and your content otherwise; `pending` shows the data of the last `success` (`keepPreviousData`, default true), else `placeholderData`, with `aria-busy` and a small spinner, and loading when neither is there or both are empty. `data` is read only with `success`: an initial value passed while pending (an `[]` default, a cache guess) never counts as a result, so the first load always shows loading; pass it as `placeholderData` to show it busy instead. Pass `fetching` for libraries whose status stays `success` during a refetch. `isEmpty` decides what counts as empty (an empty array, `null` or `undefined` by default). Every state takes `size`: `inline`, `panel` (default) or `page`.

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: Presentational keyboard key and key group rendered as kbd.

items.name: shortcuts
items.title: Shortcuts
items.description: Keyboard shortcuts on UI SDK's shared shortcuts: useShortcut with scopes, sequences (g i) and mod, ShortcutScope for a region or an open panel, ShortcutHint drawn with Kbd. Plain keys never fire while typing or composing.
items.docs: `useShortcut(keys, handler, { scope, enabled, description, allowInInput, when, layer })` registers while mounted. Keys are `+`-joined (`mod+k`, `shift+?`), a space makes a two-step sequence (`g i`, 1.2 s apart at most), and `?` matches with or without Shift. Plain keys never run while focus is in an input, textarea or contenteditable, nor during IME composition. `<ShortcutScope name label active>` limits the shortcuts inside it: `active="focus"` (default) while focus is within, `true` while mounted (an open side panel), and inside a dialog they belong to that dialog. `ShortcutHint keys` draws the keys with `Kbd` (aria-hidden; give the control `aria-keyshortcuts`, which `useAriaKeyshortcuts` returns for single steps). `Button shortcut` and `DropdownMenuItem shortcut` bind and show a key. Shortcuts are a people-only accelerator: agents already press the same parts by name, so they gain nothing new.

items.name: shortcuts-dialog
items.title: Shortcuts Dialog
items.description: A ? dialog that lists the shortcuts available where the person is, grouped by ShortcutScope.
items.docs: Mount `<ShortcutsDialog />` once. `?` opens it, however the layout types it (`shortcut` changes or, with `null`, removes the key). Touch screens have no `?`, so give it a way in: `<ShortcutsDialog><ShortcutsDialogTrigger>Keyboard shortcuts</ShortcutsDialogTrigger></ShortcutsDialog>` (a `Button` look; it lists the shortcuts of the `ShortcutScope` it sits in), or control it with `open`/`onOpenChange` from a button elsewhere. It reads `listShortcuts()` as it opens, before the modal pauses the page's shortcuts, and lists only shortcuts with a `description`, grouped by scope under each `ShortcutScope label`. `extra` adds rows that aren't registered shortcuts, like a list's own j/k keys. `labels` (`title`, `global`, `open`, `description`) in the page's language; English by default.

items.name: table
items.title: Table
items.description: Semantic table parts with aria-sort-ready headers and a horizontal scroll area on narrow screens. Cells stay on one line, cut with an ellipsis and a title holding the whole text while they overflow; TableCell wrap lets one wrap.
items.docs: `TableCell` keeps its text on one line, up to `max-w-80`, with an ellipsis; when the pointer arrives at a cell that is cut off, its `title` becomes the whole text (a `title` you pass stays). `wrap` drops the limit and wraps the text onto more lines instead, for descriptions and summaries. Screen readers and agents always get the whole text.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: UI SDK Tooltip parts: names or describes its trigger, opens on hover and keyboard focus, Escape closes it, optional shortcut and arrow. ControlTooltip gives an icon-only control its name in a tooltip.
items.docs:
### Icon buttons

You rarely write a tooltip for an icon button: `Button`, `Toggle` and the button-like triggers with `size="icon"` show their `aria-label` in one, with the shortcut keys, and close, clear, step and toolbar buttons across the registry do the same. `ControlTooltip` is the helper behind them, for a control of your own: `<ControlTooltip label="Next">{nextButton}</ControlTooltip>`. It labels the control when its text repeats the name and describes it otherwise, hides itself from agents (`agentPressable` lists it, for a trigger that isn't an agent component of its own), skips touch, a natively disabled control and one that is `aria-hidden`, and takes `tooltip={false}`, a string or `{ content, side, align }`. Write the parts yourself for anything else: a hint on a text button, a shared tooltip with a controller, or a toggleable info button.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: UI SDK Popover parts on a glass-ready surface: focus moves in, Escape and outside presses close it, focus returns to the trigger.

items.name: floating
items.title: Floating
items.description: A container that sticks to an edge of its nearest container (sticky, fixed or absolute), on the floating elevation: logical sides, safe-area insets, no viewport units. Put UI SDK controls inside, such as a Toolbar.

items.name: drawer
items.title: Drawer
items.description: UI SDK Drawer parts: a modal sheet from any edge (bottom or side), draggable, with focus trap, Escape and focus restore.
items.docs: `DrawerContent` returns focus like `DialogContent` (see the Dialog docs): also when the drawer unmounts while open or a field has `autoFocus`; prefer `initialFocus`. Its closing backdrop and content are `pointer-events: none`, but in UI SDK 0.1.0-beta.5 the drawer itself still cancels a press on the page while it slides out, so a click in that moment is lost.

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown Menu
items.description: UI SDK Menu parts with a button trigger: arrow keys, typeahead, checkbox and radio items, submenus, destructive items and async actions.
items.docs: `DropdownMenuItem shortcut` shows the keys, as UI SDK does, and presses the item when they're pressed while its menu is open (ahead of typeahead). For keys that work while the menu is closed, use UI SDK's data menus (`items`) or `useShortcut`.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: UI SDK toasts: ToastStack renders a styled, announced region with a tone icon per type; toast() and createToaster() add toasts with actions, cancel and timed dismissal.
items.docs: Place `<ToastStack />` once. Its close buttons are named `Dismiss`: pass `labels={{ close: "…" }}` in the page's language. Each type shows a decorative icon in its tone colour (a spinner while loading, none for `default`); the text still has to say what happened. Only the toasts take pointer events, and timers pause on focus or a pointer resting `hoverDelay` ms (300). In tests, find toasts with `[data-slot="toast"]` or `@eskais/test-utils`, not page-wide text: UI SDK copies each toast into a live region that outlives it.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: UI SDK Select: trigger, popup list, items with a check indicator, groups and separators, or `options` as data with a clearable none choice. Works inside Field; agents choose by label.
items.docs: Pass `options` (`{ value, label, disabled?, description? }[]`, or groups `{ label, options }[]`) and leave out children: the trigger, list, groups and indicators render for you, and the labels are known before the list opens. `placeholder` shows while nothing is selected. `clearable="No team"` adds a first choice with that label that sets the value to `null` (single selects only). `size="sm"` gives the trigger a compact fixed height for toolbars and filters (keep `default` with a floating label), and `triggerProps` (`id`, `className`, `data-*`, `size`, which wins) go to the trigger. `SelectTrigger size` does the same with parts. Outside a Field, name it with `aria-label`. With children, the parts API works as before, and `options` still feeds the root's `items`.

items.name: native-select
items.title: Native Select
items.description: A styled native <select> for mobile-heavy forms, with the same options shape as Select, a placeholder and a clearable none choice. A small primitive reports it to agents, which a bare <select> is not.
items.docs: `<NativeSelect options placeholder clearable value onValueChange name required>` inside a `Field`: the platform's own picker, which suits touch screens and long lists better than a popup. `options` takes Select's shape (`{ value, label, disabled? }` and groups `{ label, options }`, rendered as `<optgroup>`); values are strings, and `null` means nothing chosen. Native `required` and form submission work as usual. UI SDK ships no part for a native select, and its agent bridge lists only UI SDK parts, so a bare `<select>` or a `FieldControl` is invisible to agents. NativeSelect renders through its own primitive (`native-select`, `closed`) that lists its choices and takes `setValue` by label or value; an unknown choice is refused with the real ones. Inside a `FormField` it binds like Select.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: UI SDK Combobox: a filtering input with clear and trigger buttons and a popup list. Works inside Field; agents choose by label.

items.name: segmented-control
items.title: Segmented Control
items.description: UI SDK SegmentedControl: one choice from a row of buttons with a sliding indicator, like a board/table view switch.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: UI SDK Checkbox and CheckboxGroup: checked, unchecked and indeterminate, labelled by Field.

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: UI SDK Textarea: multi-line field with auto resize and a submit shortcut, labelled by Field.

items.name: token-input
items.title: Token Input
items.description: UI SDK Token Input styled as a field: removable token chips with undo, Backspace and arrow keys, and a labels mode where Enter or a comma commits and a paste splits; agents set it by label.
items.docs: `<TokenInput tokenType="label" value onValueChange validate max tone labels>` with a `<TokenInputEditor placeholder>` child, inside a `Field` or `FormField`: a list of labels as removable chips. Enter or a comma turns the typed text into a label, a paste splits on commas and line breaks, Backspace removes the chip before the caret and Ctrl/Cmd+Z brings it back. The value is `string[]` (readonly arrays welcome). Without `tokenType`, the value is UI SDK's mix of text and tokens (`TokenInputValue`), for mentions or files: pass `renderToken` and a `TriggerMenu` child as UI SDK documents. The remove buttons are pointer-only and named by `labels.remove` ("Remove {label}").

items.name: quantity
items.title: Quantity
items.description: Honest values: formatQuantity() and QuantityValue show unknown as a dash, estimated with ~ and screen reader text, and the source in the title.

items.name: relative-time
items.title: Relative Time
items.description: formatRelative() and formatInstant() on Date + Intl, a RelativeTime <time> with the absolute instant in its title, and a useNow hook that pauses while the page is hidden.

items.name: acceptance-list
items.title: Acceptance List
items.description: A list of pass, fail and unverified criteria with evidence, and a segmented AcceptanceBar on the UI SDK Meter with an accessible summary.

items.name: stat
items.title: Stat
items.description: Summary figures: Stat, StatLabel, StatValue (a number, a Quantity or a node), StatHint and StatDelta (a change with its direction in words), in a responsive StatGroup list.
items.docs: `<StatDelta value comparison invert direction tone format locale labels>` shows a change beside a value: an arrow (mirrored in right to left) and the size of the change in a soft tone chip, then `comparison` ("vs. last week", your words). `value` is a ratio by default (0.12 reads "12%"); `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options or a function. Its sign gives the direction (zero is flat) and the direction the tone: up is success, down destructive, flat neutral; `invert` swaps them for a metric where down is good, like cost. The arrow and colour are hidden from screen readers, which hear `labels.up/down/flat(formatted)` ("up 12%") and then the comparison, so the meaning never rests on colour or the icon. Override the labels in the page's language.

items.name: description-list
items.title: Description List
items.description: Terms and their details in a dl: stacked, inline (side by side, stacked again in a narrow container) or a grid of columns. Spacing from the role tokens, copyable details with an agent copy action, and a dash for an empty value that screen readers read as an overridable label.
items.docs: `<DescriptionList layout columns labels>` renders a `dl` of `DescriptionItem`s, each a `div` holding a `DescriptionTerm` (`dt`) and its `DescriptionDetails` (`dd`). `layout="stacked"` (default) puts each term above its details, `gap-group` between items; `"inline"` puts them side by side, the term at `--description-term-width` (33%), divided by rules, and stacks them again once the list's own width drops under 24rem (a container query, so it works in a side panel); `"grid"` lays the items out in as many columns as fit at `--description-column-min` (12rem), never more than `columns` (3). Spacing comes from the role tokens, so `data-theme="compact"` tightens it. An empty `DescriptionDetails` (nothing, `null` or `""`) shows an `aria-hidden` dash and reads `labels.empty` ("Not set"). `mono` sets the value in the monospace face (ids, hashes). `copyable` adds a copy button after the value (`copyValue` when the details aren't plain text, `onCopy`), as CodeBlock does: the value is a group named by its term with a `copy` action for agents, the button is hidden from them, and "Copied" (`labels.copied`) is announced. Override `labels={{ empty, copy, copied }}` in the page's language.

items.name: board
items.title: Board
items.description: Generic kanban layout: a named, horizontally scrolling list of columns with headers, counts, actions, collapsible columns agents can toggle by name, groups and an empty slot.

items.name: status-pill
items.title: Status Pill
items.description: Presentational status pill with the shared tones (plus muted) and an optional dot that can pulse, and StatusDot: a coloured dot with a screen reader label. The pulse stops under reduced motion.

items.name: dependency-chips
items.title: Dependency Chips
items.description: A named list of toned chips that truncate long labels, collapse past max into a +N chip, and become UI SDK Buttons agents can press when onSelect is set.

items.name: agent-task-types
items.title: Agent task types
items.description: TaskView, AttemptView, AgentRef, UsageSummary and ThreadRef: the data contract of the agent task components, plus effectiveAgent and agentDiffers.

items.name: agent-badge
items.title: Agent Badge
items.description: Provider, model and effort of an AgentRef: compact for cards (one line, long model ids cut in the middle, full text in title) or detail for panels, with a marker when the agent that ran isn't the one requested.

items.name: liveness-indicator
items.title: Liveness Indicator
items.description: A toned dot and label for an agent's computed liveness (running pulses, suspect_dead is destructive) and the time since its last activity, with now, locale and timeZone passed through.

items.name: task-status
items.title: Task Status
items.description: TaskStatusPill, AttemptStatusPill and ContextModePill: StatusPill tones and overridable labels for agent task, attempt and context mode values, with the source thread for reuse and fork.

items.name: usage
items.title: Usage
items.description: Token, time and cost usage of an agent task: UsageStat for a card and UsageTable on Table, with compact counts, the exact value in the title, honest unknown and estimated values, and summaries side by side as columns.

items.name: attempt-timeline
items.title: Attempt Timeline
items.description: An agent task's attempts on the UI SDK Timeline: kind, status, times, configured and executed route with earlier routes in a popover, context, repairs, checks, commits, blockers, thread links agents can press, usage per attempt and older attempts behind a toggle.

items.name: agent-task-board-core
items.title: Agent Task Board core
items.description: The non-visual core of AgentTaskBoard: filter, group, sort and summarize tasks; English and Spanish labels; and the board and proposals primitives whose agent actions select, filter, switch views, open threads and decide proposals.

items.name: proposal-actions
items.title: Proposal Actions
items.description: Approve and Reject for one task proposal: async pending with no double submit, inline errors, an on-screen reject confirmation, and agent access set by agentApproval (confirm, allow or deny). Renders nothing in snapshot mode.

items.name: task-card
items.title: Task Card
items.description: A compact agent task card: id, two-line title, profile, active agent, liveness, acceptance bar, attempts and cost, dependency chips, blocker with its retry time, decision and analysis-mode markers, and proposal actions in live mode. A stretched UI SDK Button selects it without nesting other controls.

items.name: task-detail-panel
items.title: Task Detail Panel
items.description: An agent task's goal, acceptance and evidence, dependencies that select their task, the pending decision with proposal actions, usage and the attempt timeline. TaskDetailPanel shows it as a non-modal panel; TaskDetailDialog as a modal dialog or a right-side drawer. Escape and a close button close either.

items.name: agent-task-board
items.title: Agent Task Board
items.description: The full board for AI agent tasks: filters, search, a board or sortable table view, a summary, collapsible status columns with ready and waiting groups, a detail dialog, drawer or side panel, compact density on narrow hosts, snapshot and live modes, English and Spanish labels, and agent actions to select, filter, switch views, open threads and decide proposals.

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: UI SDK Accordion parts: triggers in headings, Enter and Space toggle, animated panels on the density tokens.

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover Card
items.description: UI SDK Hover Card on the popover surface: a link that previews where it goes on hover or keyboard focus.

items.name: context-menu
items.title: Context Menu
items.description: UI SDK Menu opened by right-click, long press or Shift+F10 on a focusable area, with the dropdown menu's items.

items.name: menubar
items.title: Menubar
items.description: UI SDK Menubar: one tab stop, arrow keys between menus, with the dropdown menu's surface and items.

items.name: navigation-menu
items.title: Navigation Menu
items.description: UI SDK Navigation Menu: a named landmark of triggers that disclose panels of links, each panel on the popover surface.

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb
items.description: Presentational breadcrumb trail: a navigation named Breadcrumb, an ordered list and aria-current on the current page.

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: UI SDK Pagination that works standalone: page, pageCount or total and pageSize, onPageChange with details, overridable labels.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: UI SDK Command list with search, groups, empty state and Kbd shortcuts, plus a CommandDialog palette with an opt-in mod+K trigger.
items.docs: For a ⌘K palette: `<CommandDialog><CommandDialogTrigger shortcut="mod+k">Search<CommandDialogShortcut /></CommandDialogTrigger><CommandDialogContent title="Search"><Command onAction={…}>…</Command></CommandDialogContent></CommandDialog>`. The shortcut is opt-in, focus returns to the trigger that opened it, and `onOpenChange` reports both ways. For results from a server, use `useAsyncOptions` from `@ui-sdk/react/async-options` with `filter={false}`, `status` and `CommandStatus`; the skill's "Global search" recipe has the whole pattern. `createCommandDialogController()` opens it from code. For a second way in, like a Topbar's `centerCompact` icon, use `<CommandDialogOpenButton controller={…} aria-label="Search">`, not a second trigger: in UI SDK 0.1.0-beta.5 a second `CommandDialogTrigger` drops the dialog's agent label.

items.name: radio-group
items.title: Radio Group
items.description: UI SDK RadioGroup and Radio: pick one with arrow keys, named by Field.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: UI SDK Switch with its thumb: an on/off setting that sits in a row beside its Field label.

items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.description: UI SDK Slider: one value or a range, with a formatted value part, named by Field.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.description: UI SDK Toggle: a button that stays pressed, with variants and sizes.

items.name: toggle-group
items.title: Toggle Group
items.description: UI SDK ToggleGroup: toggles sharing one value with arrow-key focus, named by Field.

items.name: otp-input
items.title: OTP Input
items.description: UI SDK OTPInput: one native input shown as slots, with paste and one-time-code autofill.

items.name: number-input
items.title: Number Input
items.description: UI SDK NumberInput: typed, stepped and formatted numbers with step buttons, named by Field.

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description: UI SDK Label: names any control by htmlFor, including a radio group, slider or switch.

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.description: UI SDK Progress: a task's progress, determinate or indeterminate, with label and value.
items.docs: The value reads in the page's locale by default, as CLDR writes it: es-ES, fr-FR and de-DE put a no-break space (U+00A0) before the percent sign ("21 %"), en-US none. `format` on the root (`Intl.NumberFormat` options, or a function of the value) changes the visible value and what screen readers hear together, and `locale` pins the locale. `formatValue={(value, { min, max, percent, text }) => …}` on the Value part replaces only the visible value (a node, so it can hold markup), while screen readers keep the root's text; use `getValueLabel` on the root to change theirs. While the bar is indeterminate `value` and `percent` are null.

items.name: meter
items.title: Meter
items.description: UI SDK Meter: a reading within a known range, like storage used, as a bar or a ring gauge.
items.docs: The value reads in the page's locale by default, as CLDR writes it: es-ES, fr-FR and de-DE put a no-break space (U+00A0) before the percent sign ("21 %"), en-US none. `format` on the root (`Intl.NumberFormat` options, or a function of the value) changes the visible value and what screen readers hear together, and `locale` pins the locale. `formatValue={(value, { min, max, percent, text }) => …}` on the Value part replaces only the visible value (a node, so it can hold markup), while screen readers keep the root's text; use `getValueLabel` on the root to change theirs. `variant="ring"` on `Meter` with a `MeterRing size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) child draws the reading as a ring with the value in the centre (`children` replaces it) and the label below; the root keeps `role="meter"`, the ring is `aria-hidden`, `tone` colours the arc, it fills the other way round in right to left, and its transition stops under reduced motion.

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: Presentational alert with the shared tones (neutral, info, success, warning, destructive), a trailing action slot, long text that wraps, and an opt-in live role.
items.docs: Put an optional icon (`aria-hidden`), `AlertTitle` and `AlertDescription` inside. `action` takes a trailing Button; it moves below the text when the alert is narrower than 28rem. An alert is not a live region by default: pass `live` for one that appears after the page loads, and it becomes `role="alert"` for warning and destructive tones and `role="status"` otherwise. `announce` still works and is deprecated.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.description: UI SDK Calendar: a month grid with arrow, Page Up/Down and Home/End keys, single, multiple or range selection, several months, min/max and unavailable dates, locale and timeZone.

items.name: date-picker
items.title: Date Picker
items.description: UI SDK Date Picker: type a date in the locale's format or pick it from a calendar popup, single or range, with a format hint, an optional clear button and ISO values.

items.name: date-time-picker
items.title: Date Time Picker
items.description: A date from the calendar and a time of day as one local "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm" value, composed from UI SDK DatePicker and TimeInput, with min/max, a time zone suffix and locale formatting.
items.docs: `<DateTimePicker value onValueChange min max locale timeZone labels>` inside a `Field`: the field's label names the date and `labels.time` ("Time" by default) names the time, which sits in its own inner Field so the two never share an id or a name. Keep the time's label free of the date label's words (agents match labels by their words, so "Departure" and "Departure time" collide). The value is a local `"2026-11-02T14:30"`; `onValueChange` runs once both parts are set, and with `null` when either is cleared. `min`/`max` take the same shape: the date picker stops at their dates, and the time input at their times on those days. `timeZone` shows the zone's short name after the time, describes the time input and sets the calendar's today; the value stays local. `locale` sets the date format and the clock (`hourCycle` overrides it). `name` submits the combined value. Inside a `FormField` it binds like any other control. `TimeInput` is exported, styled, for a time on its own.

items.name: carousel
items.title: Carousel
items.description: UI SDK Carousel: native scroll-snap slides with Previous and Next, arrow keys, indicators and optional rotation; CarouselStatus shows "1 of 3" and useCarouselState reads the page and count; agents page it by name.

items.name: resizable
items.title: Resizable
items.description: UI SDK Resizable: panels with named separator handles that move with the pointer or arrow keys, collapse with Enter and can save their layout.

items.name: sidebar
items.title: Sidebar
items.description: App navigation: a named landmark with groups and items (href or a router link), the current page marked with aria-current, collapsing to an icon rail with tooltips (or hiding, with collapse="hide") and opening in a drawer on narrow screens. Agents collapse and expand it by name. A SidebarTrigger toggles it from elsewhere, like a Topbar, through its controller; useSidebarState wires both and remembers the state.
items.docs: Put a `SkipLink` first in `<body>`, before the `Sidebar`, so keyboard users can jump past the navigation, and give the page content the target: `<SkipLink>Skip to content</SkipLink><Sidebar …/><PageLayout as="main">…</PageLayout>` (PageLayout renders `<main id="main">`). If your shell renders `<main>` itself, give it `id="main"` (and `tabIndex={-1}`, so the no-JavaScript fallback moves focus too), or pass the SkipLink a `target` id or ref. To toggle it from a `Topbar`, pass one `createSidebarController()` to both: `<Topbar leading={<SidebarTrigger controller={sidebar} collapsed={collapsed} />} /><Sidebar controller={sidebar} collapsed={collapsed} onCollapsedChange={setCollapsed} trigger={false}>…</Sidebar>`. `collapsed` gives the trigger `aria-expanded` and the name of the next step; without it the trigger is named "Toggle sidebar". On narrow screens it opens the Sidebar's drawer (named "Open navigation", `labels.open`), and a Sidebar with `trigger={false}` renders no drawer button of its own (`narrowTrigger` overrides that); give both the same `narrowQuery`. `useSidebarState({ storageKey })` returns the controller and the state for both, remembered in localStorage: `const sidebar = useSidebarState({ storageKey: "app-sidebar" })`, then `<SidebarTrigger {...sidebar.triggerProps} />` and `<Sidebar {...sidebar.sidebarProps} trigger={false}>`. Give a sidebar whose items have no icons `collapse="hide"`: collapsed, it slides away instead of leaving an empty rail.

items.name: data-table
items.title: Data Table
items.description: Generic typed table: sortable columns with aria-sort, optional row selection with a mixed select-all, loading and empty states, and pagination through renderPagination. Sort, selection and page are controlled or not, and agents can sort, select and page it.
items.docs: Rows are one tab stop: arrows or j/k move, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown jump, Enter calls `onRowOpen(row)`, and with `selectable` Space or x toggles the focused row; a checkbox or button inside a row keeps its own keys. Past 200 rows (`virtualize="auto"`, `estimateSize`, default 41) only the rows in view render, in `tbody` between gap rows, with `aria-rowcount` and `aria-rowindex`, a sticky header and find in page through hidden stubs. Bound its height (`className="max-h-96"`) so it scrolls inside; otherwise it scrolls with the page. A column takes `wrap` (its cells wrap onto more lines instead of truncating), `cellClassName` (classes on every body cell, such as a width) and `headerClassName` (classes on its header cell).

items.name: skip-link
items.title: Skip Link
items.description: A link to the main content that stays hidden until it takes keyboard focus, then floats at the top start of the viewport above everything else.
items.docs: Render it first in `<body>`: `<SkipLink>Skip to content</SkipLink>`. The text is required (write it in the page's language). `target` is the element to skip to, an id or a ref, and defaults to `"main"`, which `PageLayout as="main"` provides. Activating the link focuses the target (giving it `tabIndex={-1}` if it can't take focus) and scrolls it into view without changing the URL, so a hash router keeps its route. It is still a real `<a href="#main">` (`#` plus the id; pass `href` for a ref target), which works without JavaScript and for a middle or modified click; it only prevents the default when it could focus the target. See the Sidebar docs for where it goes in an app shell.

items.name: page-layout
items.title: Page Layout
items.description: A page's column: centered at a dense (73.75rem), wide (90rem) or full width, with page gutters and gap-section between blocks, a header slot, and a workspace variant without padding for app-like screens.
items.docs: `<PageLayout header={<PageHeader … />}>…</PageLayout>`. It renders a `div` by default, because the app shell often owns `<main>`; pass `as="main"` when the page is the main content, and it renders `<main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>` (pass `id` to change it) so a SkipLink reaches it. The SkipLink focuses it by id without touching the URL, so hash-routed apps keep their route; with a custom `id`, pass the same value as the SkipLink's `target`. It is never a live region: announce changes from the component that changes (an Alert with `live`, a DataState). `variant="workspace"` drops the gutters and the width cap, for screens that lay out their own panes.

items.name: page-header
items.title: Page Header
items.description: Presentational page header: an eyebrow, a title at the heading level you choose, a description, an actions slot that wraps below the title on narrow screens, a breadcrumb slot and a tabs slot.
items.docs: The title is an `h1` by default (`headingLevel` changes it) with a generated id, or `titleId`, for `aria-labelledby`. `eyebrow` is a small uppercase kicker above it. `tabs` takes a `TabsList` under the title row: wrap the page in `Tabs` so the list and its `TabsPanel`s share a root, and name the list with `aria-label`.

items.name: site-header
items.title: Site Header
items.description: A floating pill header for public sites: brand, a named navigation whose links move into a More panel as the bar narrows (measured, in order, no breakpoint), dropdowns for grouped links, calls to action, and a drawer with every link on narrow screens. It sets data-scrolled once the page scrolls.
items.docs: Put a `SkipLink` first in ``, then the header: `Skip to content…} items={[{ label: "Pricing", href: "/pricing", current: true }, { label: "Solutions", items: […] }]} actions={} />…`. `renderLink={(item) => }` (or `render` per item) uses your router's link. It sticks `--floating-offset` below the top of its scroll container; set `--site-header-width` to change its 64rem cap. `moreLabel`, `menuLabel` and `closeLabel` are English by default. Style the scrolled state with `group-data-scrolled/site-header:`.

items.name: topbar
items.title: Topbar
items.description: The header of an application screen: full width and sticky, a bottom border instead of a shadow, leading (a SidebarTrigger or a breadcrumb), centre (search or a command trigger) and trailing slots, and an optional brand. The centre collapses to `centerCompact` on narrow screens. Glass gives it a translucent chrome fill.
items.docs: `<Topbar brand={…} leading={<SidebarTrigger controller={sidebar} collapsed={collapsed} />} center={<CommandDialogTrigger controller={search} shortcut="mod+k">Search</CommandDialogTrigger>} centerCompact={<CommandDialogOpenButton controller={search} variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Search">…</CommandDialogOpenButton>} trailing={<UserMenu />} />`. It renders `<header>`, which is the page's banner when it isn't inside `<main>` or a section. It sticks to the top of its scroll container; in a shell that owns the scroll (`fixed inset-0 flex flex-col`, the content `overflow-y-auto`), it simply sits first.

items.name: mobile-nav
items.title: Mobile Nav
items.description: A bottom tab bar for narrow screens: a named navigation of up to five links with the icon above the label, aria-current on the current page, an optional badge, and More, which opens the rest above the bar. Fixed to the bottom above the safe area, 56px targets, hidden above narrow: unless `always`. Glass gives it a translucent chrome fill.
items.docs: Pair it with a `Sidebar`: the sidebar on wide screens, this bar on narrow ones. `<Sidebar className="narrow:hidden" …/><PageLayout as="main" className="narrow:mb-(--mobile-nav-offset)">…</PageLayout><MobileNav label="Main" items={[{ label: "Home", href: "/", icon: <HomeIcon />, current: true }, …]} overflow={[…]} />`. The page keeps `--mobile-nav-offset` (the bar's `--mobile-nav-height`, 3.5rem, plus the bottom safe area) clear so nothing hides under it; add `viewport-fit=cover` to the viewport meta for the safe area to apply. Past five items, or with `overflow`, the fifth slot is More (`moreLabel`, English by default, and `moreIcon`). `renderLink` or `render` per item takes your router's link. It never uses viewport units.

items.name: filter-bar
items.title: Filter Bar
items.description: A UI SDK Toolbar of filters with one tab stop and arrow keys, a search field inside it, and a reset button that shows while filters apply.

items.name: chart
items.title: Chart
items.description: Recharts v3 composed with Eskais tokens: ChartContainer maps a config to --color-<key> variables (light and dark), popover tooltips and legends, and ChartDataTable renders the same data as a table for screen readers and agents. The container is a figure that requires a name.
items.docs: Categorical series use --chart-1 to --chart-5. Series with a meaning use the series tokens, which follow the theme and meet 3:1 on the background and card in both modes: --series-positive (gains, done; from --success), --series-negative (losses, failures; from --destructive), --series-target (a goal or reference line; from --foreground) and --series-remaining (what is left, a track; from --muted-foreground over --muted). Pass them as a config color, e.g. { done: { label: "Done", color: "var(--series-positive)" } }, or use the Tailwind colours (stroke-series-target). Don't rely on colour alone: add a legend or labels, and dash a target line. `ChartDataTable data labelKey keys` is generic over the row type (`TRow extends object`), so rows typed by an `interface` pass as they are and `labelKey` and `keys` must name their fields.

items.name: lightbox
items.title: Lightbox
items.description: A UI SDK Dialog that shows one image of a set: previous and next (buttons and arrow keys), a counter, the caption, an open-original link and fit or actual size. Dark variants follow the theme with no flash; agents get next, previous and goTo.
items.docs: Pass `items` ({ id, src, srcDark?, alt, name?, href? }) and control `open`/`onOpenChange` and `index`/`onIndexChange`, or put a `DialogTrigger` inside as children. `srcDark` is rendered next to `src` and CSS shows it under `.dark` or the system dark preference (unless `<html>` opts into light), so there is no flash. Focus returns to the trigger, or to whatever was focused when it opened; pass `finalFocus` to override. The dialog is sized in % of the top layer, never viewport units. Labels are English and overridable through `labels`. Agents see `Image viewer` with `next`, `previous` and `goTo(index)` (0-based).

items.name: attachments
items.title: Attachments
items.description: AttachmentStrip: a horizontally scrolling strip of image thumbnails and file chips (icon, name, type and size). Images open a Lightbox, files open their link, max adds a +N button. AttachmentThumb renders one. Agents get openAttachment(id).
items.docs: Each attachment is { id, name, kind: "image" | "file", src, srcDark?, thumbnail?, thumbnailDark?, alt, href?, size?, mimeType? }. Dark variants are rendered beside the light ones and CSS shows the one that matches the theme (`.dark`, or the system preference unless the page opted into light), so there is no flash. `onOpen(attachment, details)` runs before anything opens, for people and agents (`details.source === "agent"`); `details.cancel()` keeps it closed. Sizes are formatted with Intl in `locale`. The strip needs an `aria-label`; the other labels are English and overridable through `labels` (`open`, `more`, `lightbox`). Focus returns to the thumbnail that opened the lightbox.

items.name: stage-track
items.title: Stage Track
items.description: Where a piece of work is in a configurable pipeline (branch, PR, dev, prod): StageTrack shows every stage in a row, reached ones filled and the current one emphasised, or only the current one as a StagePill. StageFilter is a toggle group with a count per stage.
items.docs: Stages are { id, label, tone? } with the shared Tone vocabulary; a stage without a tone uses the primary colour, and StagePill defaults to info. `current` is a stage id; stages before it count as reached. The track is an ordered list with `aria-current="step"` on the current stage, and each state has its own marker shape (check, ring, hollow), so meaning never rests on colour; give it an `aria-label`. Below a 24rem container it stacks into a column. `getHref(stage)` makes a stage a link. StageFilter is a UI SDK ToggleGroup (several stages by default, `multiple={false}` for one): nothing pressed means no filter, which a segmented control can't express. Agents set it with `setValue` and stage ids.

items.name: row-navigation
items.title: Row Navigation
items.description: One tab stop over a collection's rows on UI SDK roving focus: arrows and j/k move, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown jump, Enter opens, Space and x toggle. Adds no role.
items.docs: `useRowNavigation({ ids, onOpen, onToggle, reveal })` makes the instance; wrap the rows in `RowNavigationProvider handle` and each row (a `tr`, or a row's link or button) in `NavigableRow id render`. `ids` lists every row in order, rendered or not, so Home, End and PageDown reach rows a virtualized collection hasn't rendered: `reveal(id)` scrolls one into view and focus follows when it renders. Enter calls `onOpen` only for rows that aren't links or buttons, which open themselves. Keys typed in a control inside a row stay with that control. Agents don't see it: the rows' parts and the collection's own actions already cover them.

items.name: virtual-rows
items.title: Virtual Rows
items.description: Windowed rendering for long lists and tables on TanStack Virtual, in document flow with gap rows, the focused row kept rendered, and find in page through hidden=until-found stubs.
items.docs: `useVirtualRows({ count, virtualize, estimateSize, getKey })` virtualizes past 200 rows with `virtualize="auto"`. Put `anchor` on the `ul` or `tbody`; it scrolls with the nearest scrolling ancestor, or the window. Render `segments`: rows, and gaps (`aria-hidden`) that hold the space of the rows between, so a table keeps `tbody > tr` and a list `ul > li`. Give each row `data-index` and `ref={measureElement}`. `pin(index)` keeps the focused row rendered when scrolled away; `renderNow(index)` renders one at once, for an agent's action. In each gap, `<GapFindStubs from to text offsetOf={offsetOf} onFound={scrollToIndex}>` writes the text of the rows that aren't rendered as `hidden="until-found"` elements, so find in page reaches them and scrolls the real row in; pass a stable `text(index)`.

items.name: list-item
items.title: List Item
items.description: Dense, Linear-style rows that also work as entity cards: List, ListGroup (label and count), ListItem with leading, title, subtitle, status, meta, trailing and actions, plus ListItemTitle, ListItemMeta, ListItemActions and IconTile. Agents get select(id).
items.docs: `List aria-label` holds `ListItem`s, optionally inside `ListGroup label count`. The name goes on the list itself: a `ul` (`role="list"`), or the listbox when rows are selectable, with no group around it. A row selects through a stretched link (`href`, `aria-current="page"` when `selected`) or a stretched UI SDK Button (`onSelect`), and its actions, chips and status stay their own targets. Give `List` a `value`, `defaultValue` or `onValueChange` and the rows become options of a UI SDK Listbox (arrow keys, one tab stop); options can't hold controls, so `actions` are ignored there. `variant="card"` lays rows out as cards in a responsive grid. Titles wrap to two lines, then show the full title in a tooltip; a status pill wraps below a narrow title, and trailing content and actions drop to their own line on a narrow row. `List onSelect(id, details)` runs before a row is chosen, for people and agents, and `details.cancel()` stops it. Agents see the list by its label with `select(id)`; a selectable list also shows its listbox under the same name with `setValue`, and each action resolves to one of them. Rows of a non-selectable list are one tab stop: arrows or j/k move, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown jump, Enter opens the row through its link or button, and the moved-to row scrolls into view with the least scrolling; a selectable list takes j/k and the page keys as its own arrows. Pass `items` with `renderItem` (and `getItemId`, `itemText`) to render rows from data, or give a row list `ListItem id` children directly (each child an element with a string `id`; `title` is its text), which the list reads as the same data: past 200 rows (`virtualize="auto"`, `estimateSize`) only the rows in view render, with `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset`, every row reachable by keyboard and by agents' `select`, and find in page through hidden stubs. `checkedIds` with `onCheckedIdsChange` checks rows for a bulk action: Space or x toggles the focused row, each row shows a checkbox outside the tab order (`checkLabel` names it).

items.name: side-panel
items.title: Side Panel
items.description: A non-modal inspector beside a list: a named complementary region, Escape closes it and returns focus to the row, shortcuts declared inside run while it is open, and on narrow screens it stacks below the list, overlays it or opens as a bottom sheet.
items.docs: `<SidePanel open onOpenChange title description actions returnFocus>` renders nothing while closed. Lay it out beside the list in a flex row (`--side-panel-width`, 24rem by default). `actions` (a status pill, small buttons) sit beside the title until the title would get narrower than `--card-heading-basis` (11rem), then wrap below it, as `CardHeader`'s do; the close button keeps its corner. `narrow` sets what happens at the `narrow:` breakpoint (760px and below): `"stack"` (default) keeps it in the page flow, full width, and makes its flex parent wrap so it goes below the list; `"overlay"` covers its positioned parent, as it always did before; `"sheet"` opens it as a modal bottom `Drawer` that takes focus and returns it to `returnFocus()` on close. `stack` is the default because it is the only mode that neither hides the page nor traps focus, so a panel that is open on load still leaves the list readable and reachable. Use `overlay` to show the panel instead of the list (a tall scroller in a bounded column, as the `inbox` block does), and `sheet` for a detail that should read as a step away from the list. Escape anywhere on the page closes it (a modal above it gets Escape first), and focus that was inside it, or lost to the body, moves to `returnFocus()`. It is a `ShortcutScope` that is active while open (`scope`, `scopeLabel` for the `ShortcutsDialog`), so `Button shortcut="u"` inside it works while focus stays in the list. `labels={{ close }}` names the close button.

items.name: lint-rules
items.title: Lint Rules (optional)
items.description: Optional oxlint config for Eskais UI consumers: the React, React Compiler and spacing-token presets of @p-otero/oxlint-rules, the @shadcn/lint design-system rules and eskais/icon-button-needs-label (an icon-only Button or Toggle takes size="icon" and an aria-label, so it shows a tooltip). Extend it from your .oxlintrc.json.

items.name: markdown-view
items.title: Markdown View
items.description: Renders Markdown (CommonMark, GFM tables, tasks and strikethrough, [[wikilinks]] and ![[embeds]]) to React elements with the Lezer parser, fenced code as a highlighted CodeBlock: raw HTML shows as text, only http, https, mailto and tel links become links, leading YAML frontmatter is hidden or shown as properties, and each top-level block is memoised so long notes re-render only what changed. Also extractHeadings for an outline and parseFrontmatter.
items.docs: Wikilinks: `resolveWikilink(target)` returns `{ exists, label }` (an unresolved link is dashed), `wikilinkHref(target)` its address, and `onWikilinkClick(target, event)` takes plain clicks and agents' `follow` for client routing (modified clicks stay with the browser). A wikilink with an address renders through `Link`, so it follows on press and hash routes (`#/note/x`) work; one without an address but with `onWikilinkClick` is a button. Both carry `data-wikilink` (`link` or `embed`) and `data-target`. Embeds: `![[target]]` and `![[target|alias]]` render `renderEmbed(target, alias)`, as a block when the embed is alone in its paragraph; without it, a dashed link-like chip. Frontmatter: a `---` block on the first line, closed by `---` or `...`, is hidden by default (`frontmatter="hide"`), a `<dl>` of its `key: value` lines and lists with `frontmatter="properties"` (named by `frontmatterLabel`, "Properties"), or its YAML with `"raw"`; `renderFrontmatter({ raw, properties, from, to })` draws your own. `parseFrontmatter(markdown)` reads it without a YAML dependency: plain `key: value` lines, `- item` and `[a, b]` lists, `|` and `>` blocks; nested maps are skipped, and `raw` is there for a real YAML parser. `extractHeadings(markdown)` lists `{ level, text, line, from, to, textFrom }`, frontmatter and code left out, for an outline. Keep the callbacks stable (module-level or `useCallback`): a new function re-renders every block.

items.name: markdown-editor
items.title: Markdown Editor
items.description: A Markdown editor on CodeMirror 6 with a Typora-like live preview: the document is the Markdown text, so loading and saving keep every byte. Marks show only while the caret is inside their span; headings, bullets and quotes never show theirs; tables render as tables off the caret; frontmatter stays as written. Slash and [[ menus, a one-row toolbar with an overflow menu, a ref handle for host menus and outlines, English and Spanish labels, and agent actions (getMarkdown, insertText, replaceSelection, insertWikilink, toggleFormat, setHeading, toggleTask; setMarkdown needs approval).
items.docs: The value is plain Markdown: `value`/`onChange` (debounced by `changeDelay`, 300 ms; flushed on blur and unmount) or `defaultValue`. Loading never fires `onChange`. A `value` that arrives while edits are still waiting for `onChange` calls `onConflict({ local, remote })`: return the text to keep, or nothing to take the remote; without it the local text goes out through `onChange` first and then the remote applies. A `ref` gets a `MarkdownEditorHandle` once the editor mounts (`null` before): `focus()`, `getValue()`, `getSelection()` and `setSelection(anchor, head?)` in offsets of the Markdown string, `insertText`, `insertWikilink(target, alias?)`, `insertLink(href, text?)`, `wrapSelection(before, after?)`, `runCommand(name)` for the toolbar's formats and levels (`bold`, `quote`, `taskList`, `heading2`, `paragraph`…), `scrollToLine(line)` and `getScrollLine()`; writes return `false` when read-only, and no CodeMirror type is part of it. Line commands (toolbar, slash menu, handle) leave the caret after the marker they add. Wikilinks and `![[embeds]]`: Ctrl/Cmd+click, or Enter inside one, calls `onWikilinkClick(target, event)` (and `onOpenWikilink(target)`); `embedPreview` shows an embed off the caret as `renderEmbed(target, alias)` or a placeholder. A leading `---` YAML block stays as written, in a muted monospace block. The slash menu stays open with `labels.noMatches` while nothing matches, until Escape or a space. Code languages are opt-in: `npx shadcn add @eskais/markdown-editor-languages` and pass `codeLanguages={markdownCodeLanguages}`. Pass `cspNonce` under a strict Content Security Policy (CodeMirror injects a style element). Spanish labels: `labels={markdownEditorLabelsEs}`. Shortcuts: Mod+B/I/E, Mod+Shift+X, Mod+Alt+0..6 for paragraph and heading levels, Tab/Shift+Tab to nest list items, Mod+Enter to toggle a task; Escape then Tab leaves the editor. Installing it also installs `@eskais/dropdown-menu` (the toolbar's menus: `DropdownMenu`, `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuItemIcon`, `DropdownMenuItemIndicator`, `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`), with `button`, `input`, `popover` and `tooltip`, into your `ui` folder. If you already have a `dropdown-menu.tsx` there, shadcn asks before overwriting it: keeping yours means the toolbar imports your file, so it must export those parts with the same props, or the editor breaks at build time. Add with `--overwrite`, or put your own menu under another name.

items.name: markdown-editor-languages
items.title: Markdown Editor Languages
items.description: Every code language CodeMirror knows, for MarkdownEditor's fenced code blocks; each language loads the first time a block names it. Opt-in, since the list adds about 230 KB of shared chunks to most bundles.

items.name: link
items.title: Link
items.description: Text link with inline, nav, muted, standalone and plain variants: underlined at rest or on hover so it never relies on colour, external and new-tab handling, aria-current, render for router links, an opt-in onFollow that routes plain clicks and gives agents a follow action, and fast navigation on a primary mouse press (fast={false} or data-no-fast-link to opt out); FastLinkRegion and useFastLink do the same for plain anchors.
items.docs: Same-origin links follow on a primary mouse press (`pointerdown`), for navigation only: `fast={false}` opts a link out, `data-no-fast-link` on an ancestor a region or the app. Hash routers work too: an `href` that starts with `#/` follows on press, through `onFollow` or by setting `location.hash`, while any other `#…` href is an in-page anchor and stays native. Set another prefix with `data-fast-link-hash-prefix` on an ancestor (`<body data-fast-link-hash-prefix="#!/">`) or `FastLinkRegion hashPrefix`; an empty value makes every `#…` href an anchor.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code Block
items.description: CodeBlock and CodeTabs: syntax highlighting for ts, tsx, js, jsx, json, css, html, bash, md and diff with Lezer parsers loaded on first use, rendered as React elements in syntax tokens that hold 4.5:1; a filename header, copy (an agent action too), line numbers, highlighted lines, wrap and a max height. Code for inline code.

items.name: hero
items.title: Hero
items.description: The top of a landing page: an eyebrow chip, a title with an optional muted second line, a description, actions, a copyable install command and an aside for a live demo, side by side or centered by container width, over a token-drawn grid or glow.

items.name: section-heading
items.title: Section Heading
items.description: The heading of a page section: eyebrow, a large title, a description and actions, start-aligned or centered, with the heading level and id the enclosing section names itself by.

items.name: bento
items.title: Bento
items.description: Bento and BentoTile: a container-query grid of Card tiles that spans columns on wide containers, falls to two columns and then one, and can make a whole tile a link without covering the controls inside.

items.name: steps
items.title: Steps
items.description: Steps and Step: an ordered list with numbered markers, a title, a description and any content per step, side by side on wide containers and stacked on narrow ones.

items.name: site-footer
items.title: Site Footer
items.description: A page footer: brand, description, groups of links as named navigation landmarks, and a bottom line.

items.name: docs-layout
items.title: Docs Layout
items.description: DocsLayout, an app shell for documentation: a topbar slot, a sidebar that sticks under it at the full remaining height (a drawer on narrow screens), a breadcrumb slot above the page in the main column, the main landmark and a sticky table of contents. Also DocsToc (headings marked as you read with IntersectionObserver), DocsPager and DocsBreadcrumb.
items.docs: Compose the shell from a Topbar and a Sidebar that share one controller: `const sidebar = useSidebarState({ storageKey: "docs-sidebar" })`, then `<DocsLayout topbar={<Topbar leading={<SidebarTrigger {...sidebar.triggerProps} />} brand={…} trailing={…} />} sidebar={<Sidebar label="Documentation" {...sidebar.sidebarProps} collapse="hide" trigger={false} narrowQuery="(width <= 47.5rem)">…</Sidebar>} header={<DocsBreadcrumb items={…} />} toc={<DocsToc items={headings} />}>…</DocsLayout>`. The topbar sticks to the top; the sidebar sticks under it (`top: var(--topbar-height)`) at the full remaining height and scrolls on its own; elements with an `id` in the page scroll into view below the topbar. The trigger collapses the sidebar on wide screens and opens its drawer on narrow ones. Without a `topbar`, pass `--docs-top` in `style` to clear a fixed header of your own.

items.name: shell
items.title: Shell
items.description: Shell, an application's whole frame from its routes: a skip link, a Topbar (sidebar trigger, brand, ⌘K search, actions), a grouped Sidebar that sticks under it, collapses (remembered) and is a drawer on narrow screens, a command palette whose Go to group reaches every route, a MobileNav bottom bar with More on narrow screens, and the main landmark. Router-agnostic: onNavigate for a history router, #/route hrefs for a hash router, or plain fast links.
items.docs: `<Shell routes={routes} groups={[{ id: "main", label: "Workspace" }, { id: "legacy", label: "Legacy", tone: "muted" }]} currentHref={pathname} onNavigate={(href) => router.push(href)} brand={<Logo />} actions={<UserMenu />} storageKey="app-sidebar">{page}</Shell>`, with `routes` of `{ id, label, href, icon?, group?, mobile?, keywords?, badge? }` (extend the type with your own fields: `onNavigate` gets your route back). `currentHref` is an href or a matcher `(href) => pathname.startsWith(href)` (the longest match wins); it sets `aria-current="page"` and the primary fill in the sidebar, the bottom bar and the palette. Without `onNavigate` routes are plain links that fast links follow on press, and `#/route` hrefs work with a hash router. Routes flagged `mobile: true` (up to four) fill the bottom bar on narrow screens and More opens the rest; the bar is sticky at the end of the shell, so the page always ends above it. Translate every string with `labels` (`skipToContent`, `sidebar`, `mobileNav`, `goTo`, `more`, `openSearch`, `search`, `empty`…). Add palette commands with `commandGroups` (CommandGroups) and run them with `onCommand`. Put pages in `PageLayout` (not `as="main"`: the shell owns `<main id="main">`). Inside a pane, set `--shell-height` in `style` to the pane's height and pass `as="div"` if the page already has its `<main>`.

items.name: landing-page
items.title: Landing Page
items.description: A whole landing page made only of blocks (Hero, SectionHeading, Bento, Steps and SiteFooter, with a header slot), with its content in one object: the template to copy and edit.

items.name: icon
items.title: Icon
items.description: Icon names a lucide-react icon (or any SVG component) for screen readers: <Icon icon={TrashIcon} label="Deleted" /> renders role=img with that label. Decorative icons need no wrapper, since lucide hides them by default.
items.docs: The registry draws its icons with `lucide-react`: import them by name (`import { CheckIcon } from "lucide-react"`). Lucide sets `aria-hidden` on an icon that has no `aria-*`, `role` or `title` prop, so a decorative icon needs no wrapper. Use `Icon` only when the icon carries meaning nothing else states: `<Icon icon={TriangleExclamationPointIcon} label="Blocked" />` renders `role="img"` with that `aria-label`. Size comes from the parent (Button, Badge, menu items and inputs set `[&_svg]:size-4`) or a `size-*` class: `size-3.5` beside `text-body-sm`, `size-4` beside `text-body`, `size-5` beside a title; our classes override lucide's `size` prop. Colour is `currentColor`: set a text colour, like `text-success`.

items.name: inbox
items.title: Inbox
items.description: A keyboard-first inbox block: a virtualized List of messages, j/k and Enter to open a SidePanel inspector with single-key actions, x to select for a bulk action and ? for every key.

items.name: master-detail
items.title: Master Detail
items.description: MasterDetail: a list with a detail pane, side by side on wide containers and stacked below 42rem with a Back button. Controlled or uncontrolled selection, optional URL sync through a router-agnostic adapter (hash routers included), j/k that follow focus, a detail that collapses to a rail or resizes, remembered under a storageKey, and focus that moves to the detail's heading and back to the row. Agents open and close items by the block's name.
items.docs: `<MasterDetail label="Devices" renderList={(state) => <List aria-label="Devices">{devices.map((d) => <ListItem key={d.id} title={d.name} {...state.itemProps(d.id)} />)}</List>} renderDetail={(id) => ({ title, description, actions, content })} emptyDetail={<Empty … />} />`. It fills its parent's height (`--master-detail-height`, 100% by default), so give it a bounded box, like an app shell's main column. `selectedId`, `defaultSelectedId` and `onSelectedIdChange` (cancel with `details.cancel()`); `url={createUrlParam("device")}` from `@/lib/url-param` keeps it in the URL (`{ in: "hash" }` for a hash route's query); `followFocus` opens the row that j/k move to; `collapsible`, `resizable` and `storageKey` for the detail's width. Every label is in `labels`.

items.name: dashboard-grid
items.title: Dashboard Grid
