items.description: DashboardGrid: a row of stats over a container-query grid of cards (one column, two from 42rem, `columns` from 64rem) where rows are at least one height and cards in a row share it, so they line up, keep their size from loading to loaded and grow their row rather than clip. DashboardCard spans columns and rows and loads through DataState (a skeleton, the error with Retry, an empty title); DashboardChart fills a card and is named by its title; DashboardMeter centres a ring meter in one; DashboardStats and DashboardStat (with a StatDelta in `delta`) draw placeholders of the value's height.
items.docs: `<DashboardGrid columns={3} labels={{ errorTitle, emptyTitle }} stats={<DashboardStats aria-label="This week" loading={pending}><DashboardStat label="Runs" value={261} delta={<StatDelta value={0.12} comparison="vs. last week" />} loading={pending} /></DashboardStats>}><DashboardCard title="Runs" span={2} status={query.status} data={query.data} error={query.error} onRetry={query.refetch}>{(data) => <DashboardChart config={config}><BarChart data={data}>…</BarChart></DashboardChart>}</DashboardCard></DashboardGrid>`. Rows are at least `--dashboard-row-height` (20rem) tall and cards in a row share the height; a card whose content is taller grows its row, never clips it, so set the row height to fit your cards to keep loading and loaded the same height. Without `status`, a card shows its children as they are; `DashboardMeter label value hint` centres a ring meter in it. `retry`, `loading` and `refreshing` default to English and every label is overridable on the grid or a card.

items.name: settings-page
items.title: Settings Page
items.description: SettingsPage: a section navigation that sticks beside the sections on wide containers and becomes a section picker on narrow ones, marking the section being read (IntersectionObserver). Going to a section scrolls by id and focuses its heading, so it works under hash routers; the section can live in the URL through createUrlParam. SettingsSection, SettingsRow (a label, a description and the control on the right, stacking when narrow), SettingsFacts (a DescriptionList for read-only facts) and SettingsDangerZone with SettingsDangerAction rows that confirm through ConfirmDialog and need a person's approval for agents.
items.docs: `<SettingsPage url={createUrlParam("section")} style={{ "--settings-top": "var(--topbar-height)" }}><SettingsSection id="security" title="Security" description="…" actions={…}><SettingsRow label="Two-factor authentication" description="…"><Switch /></SettingsRow></SettingsSection><SettingsSection id="device" title="This device"><SettingsFacts aria-label="This device"><DescriptionItem>…</DescriptionItem></SettingsFacts></SettingsSection><SettingsDangerZone id="danger" title="Danger zone"><SettingsDangerAction label trigger title confirmLabel agentConfirm onConfirm /></SettingsDangerZone></SettingsPage>`. The navigation lists every direct `SettingsSection` child with a text title (`navLabel` otherwise), or pass `sections`. `--settings-top` is the height of anything sticky above the page and `--settings-height` the box that scrolls it. `currentSection` and `onSectionChange` (reason `scroll`, `nav` or `url`) follow your own state. A `SettingsRow` is a `Field` that names a UI SDK control; `field={false}` for a button. Labels `nav` and `jump` are overridable.

items.name: eskais-mockup-skill
items.title: Mockup skill
items.description: Agent skill for @eskais/mockup: build a throwaway, offline HTML mockup of a screen from the project's own components in five levels (project components, uninstalled registry items, parts, UI SDK primitives with a reason, recorded gaps) and validate it. items.name: document-workspace
items.title: Document Workspace
items.description: A notes or docs workspace: an explorer, tabs, breadcrumb, toolbar, the document (edit or read), an aside for backlinks, properties and the outline, a status bar with the save state, an alert slot and Ctrl/Cmd+P quick open. Resizable, collapsible columns when its container is wide, drawers when narrow; named landmarks and toggles agents can press. Also DocumentOutline and DocumentQuickOpen.
items.docs: `<DocumentWorkspace document={mode === "edit" ? <MarkdownEditor ref={editor} …/> : <MarkdownView …/>} explorer tabs breadcrumb toolbar statusBar aside alert quickOpen={<DocumentQuickOpen items onOpen />} mode onModeChange editorRef={editor} headings={extractHeadings(markdown)} saveState storageKey>`. It fills its parent (`--document-workspace-height`, 100% by default) and decides its layout from its own width, never the viewport, so it works inside an app shell's `<main>`: at `narrow` (760 px) or less, the explorer and the aside are 20rem drawers that start closed; wider, they are resizable columns (`Resize files`, `Resize details` handles) that collapse from their toggles or the handle. `explorerOpen`/`onExplorerOpenChange` and `asideOpen`/`onAsideOpenChange` follow what is shown; turning narrow closes them and turning wide brings back the columns. `storageKey` remembers the columns' state and widths in localStorage (the drawers always start closed). Landmarks: the explorer is a `nav`, the aside an `aside`, the document a named region (`documentAs="main"` when the workspace is the page's main content); the toggles carry `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The mode switch is a SegmentedControl; switching keeps the reading position by heading (from the editor's `getScrollLine` to the read view's headings and back). `saveState` (`saved`, `saving`, `unsaved`, `error`) is a polite `<output>` in the status bar; `alert` sits in an assertive region that is always there, so a conflict is read once when it appears (pass an `Alert` without `live`). `quickOpen` adds a Quick open button and `quickOpenShortcut` (`mod+p`, `false` to turn it off). `DocumentOutline` lists `headings`: in edit mode an entry puts the caret at the heading (`setSelection`, `scrollToLine`) and focuses the editor; in read mode it scrolls to the heading and focuses it. Drawers, quick open and menus give focus back to the document unless the action moved it: pass `useDocumentWorkspace().documentFocusTarget` as `finalFocus` to your own menus in `toolbar`. `editorRef` takes any `DocumentEditor` (`focus`, `scrollToLine`, `setSelection`, `getScrollLine`), which `MarkdownEditorHandle` is. All text is in `labels`.
